content.text: Workers endure brutal hours, poverty, unsafe jobs, surveillance, wage theft, scamping, and contempt from employers and fellow workers. Socialist agitation spreads through meetings at Windley, despite violent opposition. At “The Refuge,” a worn rope breaks while raising the sixty-five-foot ladder, killing Philpot and injuring Barrington. His coffin is taken from the mortuary to his lodger’s house, then to the yard, and finally to the cemetery. The Beano exposes class servility and drunkenness. During the election, impoverished workers enthusiastically support Sweater or D’Encloseland despite receiving no benefit. Barrington rejects capitalist politics, while a former Socialist becomes a paid Liberal propagandist. After Ruth gives birth, she flees Easton’s house with her baby, attempts to reach the lake in the park, then stays at Owen’s house before taking work and living separately.
